How every story is told

Three chapters, almost like life itself

  1. Chapter I

    Back There

    Memories of the homeland, the people, and the places that shaped a soul.

    “I still remember the courtyard in Tashkent where our theater rehearsed until midnight, convinced art could outlast any empire.” — From the archive: Nabi Abdurakhmanov (3h 26m)
  2. Chapter II

    Arrival

    First steps into the unknown, filled with challenges, fears, discoveries, and small victories.

    “Landing in America in 1976 with $90 in my pocket, two suitcases of bronze tools and paintings, performing pantomime before a single word of English.” — From the archive: Grigory Gurevich (6h 0m)
  3. Chapter III

    What Now

    A moment of reflection on identity, belonging, and the dreams that carry us forward.

    “Today my students write poetry in two languages. You don’t erase your first home—you build a bridge strong enough for your children.” — From the archive: Dr. Olga Zbarskaya (55m)

        Nationwide 50-State Expansion

        Immigrant voices across all 50 US States

        Born in Brooklyn, Immimentary invites immigrants from every state in America—from Alaska to Florida, California to Maine—to leave their information and join the living documentary archive.

        How Alice works

        Alice's team

          Open call · All 50 US States

          Your story belongs in the archive

          Immimentary is more than a show. It is a cultural archive of resilience and love, and it grows one life at a time. If you came to America from somewhere else, whether last year or fifty years ago, we would like to hear from you.

          You do not need to be famous. A seamstress’s story matters as much as an Olympian’s. You can speak in English, Russian, Ukrainian, or the language you think in.

          1. Write to us. Leave your information in the 50-State Story Box with a few lines about where you are from and how you got here.
          2. We talk. The producer calls you to hear the story and plan the interview.
          3. We record. A relaxed, unhurried conversation in our Brooklyn studio, on location in your state, or via remote production.
          4. It joins the archive. Your full story is published here, on immimentary.org, and on YouTube, for your family and for history.
          50-State Archival Initiative: Every submission is indexed by US state, homeland and arrival decade for the production team.

            About the series

            Honest. Vulnerable. Unforgettable.

            REC · 06:00:20 · 4K 24FPS BROOKLYN STUDIO · TWO CHAIRS
            “Not actors. Real people speaking about the homeland they left, the day they arrived, and who they have become.” Click any portrait ↗
            CAM A · 50MM PRIME · F/1.8 ISO 800 · 5600K
            “Three chapters, almost like life itself: Back There, Arrival, What Now.”
            CH1/CH2: LAVALIER + BOOM LONGEST TAKE: 06:00:20
            The Immimentary Set (Brooklyn, NY): Two armchairs, unhurried time, and an open lens where real immigrants speak for two, three, or up to six hours.

            Immimentary is a living documentary series that gives voice to the immigrant journey in its most personal and human form. Each episode is built around one real story, told by the person who lived it, at the length it deserves. Many run two, three, or up to six hours (Grigory Gurevich).

            The archive already holds pianists and priests, Olympic athletes and Bolshoi soloists, engineers, doctors, entrepreneurs, survivors of the Siege of Leningrad, and families who arrived with nothing. Lives that may seem distant, yet remind us how deeply we are all connected.

            Greg Romenski

            Creator & producer

            A producer on Brooklyn Public Television, Greg won two prizes for his program Medcastplus (now ZurMed) in 2018 and 2022 in the “B-Healthy” category. About the award
